sections.heading: Is ACY Securities Worth Your Money in 2026?
sections.body:
Founded in Sydney in 2013, ACY Securities built its pitch around two things — raw spreads from institutional liquidity providers and fast execution under 30ms. The ASIC licence (AFSL 403863) is real, the pricing on ProZero is genuinely competitive at 0.0 pips plus $6 round-turn, and the 2,200+ CFD instrument range covers everything from forex to crypto to ETFs. For Australian residents specifically, this is a legitimate mid-range broker backed by Tier-1 regulation and proper fund segregation.

But here is what the marketing does not emphasise. If you live outside Australia, you are not getting ASIC protection. You land on ACY Capital LLC — registered in St Vincent and Grenadines, a jurisdiction with no meaningful forex regulatory framework. And four separate national regulators in France, Spain, Ukraine, and Malaysia have added ACY to their warning lists for operating without local authorisation. Not fraud warnings — but a pattern that tells you something about how aggressively this broker chases new markets.

ACY works best for Australian traders who get the full benefit of ASIC oversight. International clients should ask themselves: why choose SVG when IC Markets or Pepperstone offer identical pricing under CySEC or FCA?

sections.heading: Is ACY Securities Regulated? — Licence Check 2026
sections.body:
Yes — ACY Securities Pty Ltd holds Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) licence AFSL 403863. That is a genuine Tier-1 retail licence with real enforcement power, mandatory fund segregation in Australian Tier-1 banks, and domestic dispute resolution through the Australian Financial Complaints Authority (AFCA). For Australian residents, this is meaningful protection.

The international entity is ACY Capital LLC, registered in St Vincent and the Grenadines (Company 2610 LLC 2022). SVG does not regulate forex brokers — the FSA registration is a company incorporation, not a regulatory licence in any meaningful sense. There is no compensation scheme, no dispute resolution body, and no leverage restrictions. You get 1:500 leverage because nobody is stopping the broker from offering it.

ACY previously operated a Vanuatu entity (ACY Capital Australia Limited) under the VFSC, which has since been discontinued. The entity structure has consolidated around ASIC for locals and SVG for everyone else. Under ASIC, Australian retail clients receive 1:30 leverage on major pairs, mandatory negative balance protection, and fund segregation — but no investor compensation scheme exists under Australian law. NAFT last reviewed ACY Securities regulation in May 2026.

sections.heading: ACY Securities Spreads, Fees and Accounts — What Do You Actually Pay?
sections.body:
ProZero is the account to open if you trade actively. Raw spreads from 0.0 pips on EUR/USD — broker-stated average sits around 0.1-0.2 during London and New York sessions — with a $6 round-turn commission per standard lot. That gives you an all-in cost of roughly $7-$8 per lot, which matches or undercuts most ASIC-regulated competitors. Execution is sourced from 16 liquidity providers including JP Morgan, UBS, Credit Suisse, State Street, and Citadel, with fills within 30ms (broker-stated).

Standard account wraps everything into the spread at 0.6-1.2 pips average on EUR/USD with zero commission. Mathematically worse for active traders but simpler for position traders who hold for days and care less about entry precision. The Bespoke account offers similar raw pricing to ProZero but at AUD $5 round-turn — roughly $3.25 USD per side — making it marginally cheaper for high-volume traders who negotiate.

Leverage under ASIC is capped at 1:30 for major pairs, 1:20 for minors, and 1:10 for commodities — standard retail restrictions. Under the SVG entity, you get up to 1:500 with no tiered reduction. That is not a feature; that is how undercapitalised accounts get destroyed in minutes during volatility events. No inactivity fee is published. Swap-free Islamic accounts are available on request.

table.footnote: Spread data is broker-stated. Leverage shown as ASIC retail / SVG entity. All-in cost = (spread x $10) + commission per standard lot.

sections.heading: ACY Securities Deposits and Withdrawals — Speed and Methods
sections.body:
Deposits are instant via card and most e-wallets. Bank wire takes 1-3 business days depending on your bank. No deposit fees on any method — ACY absorbs processing costs on the way in, which is standard for competitive brokers. Minimum deposit is $50 across all methods and account types. Cryptocurrency deposits via BTC and USDT are processed after network confirmation.

The payment method selection skews heavily toward Asia-Pacific. China UnionPay, POLi (Australia/NZ), Fasapay (Southeast Asia), and Dragonpay (Philippines) are all present. But there is no Neteller, no PayPal, and no Skrill — which limits options for African, Middle Eastern, and European clients who rely on those e-wallets. If your preferred method is not on the list, bank wire is your fallback, and that means waiting days rather than minutes.

Withdrawals are stated as same-day if requested before 9PM AEST. Most methods carry no withdrawal fee — a genuine advantage over brokers charging $5-$25 per withdrawal. The free withdrawal policy removes one of the common friction points that trap capital inside broker accounts.

sections.heading: ACY Securities Withdrawals — The Real Picture in 2026
sections.body:
The same-day withdrawal policy looks good on paper, and plenty of traders report smooth processing within hours. But dig into community forums and a different pattern emerges alongside the positive experiences. Numerous traders have reported significant delays — publicly documented across multiple independent sources. The complaints are not universal, but they are consistent enough to notice.

Trustpilot shows approximately 3.8-4.0 out of 5.0 from around 200 reviews — a moderate sample size that makes it difficult to draw definitive conclusions. The rating is respectable but the review count is too low to fully validate the same-day claim at scale. Polarisation exists: satisfied traders praise the execution and pricing, while the minority of negative reviews cluster around withdrawal timing and communication during the wait.

What does this mean practically? If you deposit $500 and request a withdrawal of your balance, it will likely process same-day without issues. The complaints tend to surface around larger amounts or profits generated through specific trading patterns. Is this normal compliance friction or something more systemic? The data does not clearly answer that question — but the pattern warrants caution. Test with a small withdrawal before committing significant capital. And if a withdrawal stalls beyond 48 hours, escalate immediately through formal channels rather than waiting on live chat promises.

If a withdrawal stalls: contact support@acy.com with your withdrawal reference number, escalate to compliance if no resolution within 48 hours, and file with AFCA (Australian Financial Complaints Authority) if you are under the ASIC entity.

sections.heading: ACY Securities Red Flags — What to Know Before You Deposit
sections.body:
No evidence of outright fraud or scam operation — but several structural concerns demand attention. The dual-entity model is the primary issue: ASIC does real work protecting Australian clients, but the SVG entity covering everyone else operates in a regulatory vacuum. Four national regulators have independently flagged ACY for cross-border operations without authorisation. That is not normal for a broker with clean intentions — most well-run operations secure local licences before marketing in those jurisdictions, or simply do not accept clients from there.

The withdrawal delay complaints are not fabricated — they appear across multiple independent public sources with enough specificity to suggest real experiences rather than competitor attacks. The frequency is not overwhelming, but the pattern exists. And the discontinuation of the Vanuatu VFSC entity raises questions about why that licence was dropped rather than maintained.

None of this makes ACY a scam. The ASIC licence is real, the pricing is competitive, and plenty of traders use the platform without issues. But the risk profile is meaningfully higher for international clients than the marketing suggests. NAFT last reviewed ACY Securities in May 2026.

sections.heading: Who Should Use ACY Securities — and Who Should Not
sections.body:
ACY Securities splits cleanly along one line — are you in Australia or not? For Australian residents, this is a solid ASIC-regulated broker with competitive ProZero pricing, fund segregation, and domestic regulatory recourse through AFCA. It sits comfortably in the mid-range of Australian brokers and the $50 minimum makes it accessible without being reckless. The 2,200+ instrument range means you will not outgrow it quickly.

For international clients, the value proposition is weaker. You can get identical or better pricing from IC Markets under CySEC, or from Pepperstone under FCA — both with actual compensation schemes and regulatory teeth behind them. Choosing ACY's SVG entity over a CySEC-regulated alternative only makes sense if ACY offers something those competitors do not — and apart from Capitalise.ai automation and the specific liquidity provider mix, that case is hard to make.

sections.heading: How to Open an ACY Securities Account — Step by Step
sections.body: Registration takes under five minutes through the ACY website. Verification depends on your jurisdiction — Australian residents may experience faster KYC processing through domestic document checks. International clients should allow up to 24-48 hours for full verification.

steps.title: Register
steps.detail: Visit acy.com and click Open Live Account. Select your account type — ProZero offers the best value for active traders. Complete the application form with personal details and trading experience questionnaire. You will be assigned to either the ASIC or SVG entity based on your country of residence.

steps.title: Verify your identity (KYC)
steps.detail: Upload government-issued photo ID (passport, driving licence, or national ID card) and proof of address (utility bill or bank statement dated within 3 months). Australian residents may also need to pass an electronic ID verification check. Allow up to 24-48 hours for approval.

steps.title: Fund your account and test a withdrawal
steps.detail: Deposit the minimum $50 via your preferred method. Place a small trade to verify execution speed and spread accuracy match the ProZero claims. Then request a withdrawal immediately — confirm it processes same-day as stated before scaling up your capital. If the withdrawal clears cleanly, the pipeline works.

sections.practical_note: Deposit small. Trade once. Withdraw immediately. If the money comes back same-day with no friction, you know the process works. If anything stalls, do not deposit more until it resolves.

sections.heading: ACY Securities Final Verdict — Is It Worth It in 2026?
sections.body:
NAFT scores ACY Securities 6.0 out of 10. The ASIC licence is legitimate and the ProZero pricing — 0.0 pips plus $6 round-turn from 16 liquidity providers with sub-30ms execution — is competitive with anything on the Australian market. For traders in Australia specifically, this is a reasonable choice among several strong ASIC-regulated options. Fund segregation is real, AFCA dispute resolution is accessible, and the $50 minimum keeps the barrier low.

The score ceiling exists because of what happens outside Australia. The SVG entity that covers most international clients is regulatory theatre — registration without regulation, leverage without limits, and protection without substance. Four national regulators flagging ACY for cross-border operations tells you the growth strategy has outpaced the compliance infrastructure. And the withdrawal delay complaints, while not universal, are documented frequently enough across independent sources to prevent a higher score on that metric.

If you are an Australian resident, ACY Securities deserves consideration alongside IC Markets and Pepperstone — all three offer similar pricing under ASIC. But if you are international, NAFT recommends choosing a broker that offers genuine regulatory protection in your jurisdiction. IC Markets under CySEC or Pepperstone under FCA give you raw spreads with actual compensation schemes behind them. The question is not whether ACY is a scam — it is not. The question is whether you accept SVG oversight when better options exist at the same price point.
